newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says keeps present monetary policy for growth.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says keeps present monetary policy for growth.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday that the central bank will maintain its present monetary policy to ensure economic recovery.
He said Japan's economy is likely to withstand pressures from fiscal tightening, with private demand firming up.
"The Bank of Japan's basic monetary stance is to ensure inflation-free economic growth and to take speedy measures towards that end while monitoring money supply growth and asset prices," he said.
He said it is not proper for the BOJ to consider monetary policy in terms of addressing exchange rates and external imbalances.
Matsushita said the effects of the April 1 rise in Japan's consumption tax are now being seen, but prospects are increasing that Japan's economic recovery will continue.
"However, we have to make sure that the economic recovery will be sustained and our stance is to maintain current monetary policy to ensure economic recovery," he said.
